proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(L=1-\eta_+\).    Because \(\mathcal M_n\) is assumed nonempty, ass:uniform-shell at \(u=\lambda _0\) and ass:right-overlap imply
\[
  L>\lambda _0/2.                                                   \tag{16}
\]
Indeed, otherwise \(P\{\lambda _0/2<e(X)\leq\lambda _0\}=0\), contradicting \(c_-\lambda _0^\kappa>0\).  This also shows that \(\mathcal X\) is infinite: ass:positivity and the lower shell inequality require infinitely many positive propensity values tending to zero.  An infinite standard Borel space contains a countable measurable subset, so the countable reservoirs and their finite cell refinements below are measurable constructions on \(\mathcal X\).

We first derive the testing facts used below.  Suppose two sample laws \(Q_+\) and \(Q_-\) have targets \(t_+\) and \(t_-\) with \(|t_+-t_-|\geq2d\).  The events \(\{|T-t_+|<d\}\) and \(\{|T-t_-|<d\}\) are disjoint.  Hence, from the variational definition of total variation,
\[
 Q_+\{|T-t_+|\geq d\}+Q_-\{|T-t_-|\geq d\}
 \geq1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_+,Q_-).                                \tag{17}
\]
Thus one of the two error probabilities is at least half the right-hand side.  The same argument applies to priors.  More precisely, suppose the two mixture sample laws have total variation at most \(\gamma\), and under prior \(\theta\in\{-1,1\}\) the random target lies within \(d/4\) of a center \(\mu_\theta\), except on prior probability \(\epsilon\), where \(|\mu_+-\mu_-|=2d\).  On the target-concentration event, an estimator within \(d/2\) of the random target determines the nearer center.  Applying (17) to this induced test gives an error probability at least \((1-\gamma-2\epsilon)/2\) under one mixture.  A mixture error is an average over its fixed laws, so some fixed law in the prior support has at least that error probability.

We next make the common reservoir and its shell slack explicit.  The construction underlying def:lower-bound-handle has an untouched dyadic background and a perturbable active reservoir below a fixed number \(s_0\) satisfying
\[
 0<s_0<\min\{L,\lambda _0\}/4.                                  \tag{18}
\]
At the low scales at which the active reservoir can enter a shell, the untouched background is allocated so that
\[
 c_-u^\kappa\leq P_X\{u/2<e_0\leq u,\ \text{background}\}
 \leq2^\kappa c_-u^\kappa.                                    \tag{19}
\]
This is obtained by putting a background atom at each \(a_j=a2^{-j}\) with mass \(c_-a_{j-1}^\kappa\), where \(a\in(\lambda _0/2,\min\{L,\lambda _0\})\), and allocating the remaining, unperturbed mass on the higher dyadic cells using ass:upper-shell-richness.  For \(u\in[a_j,a_{j-1})\), exactly the atom at \(a_j\) lies in \((u/2,u]\), and therefore its mass is between \(c_-u^\kappa\) and \(2^\kappa c_-u^\kappa\).  The top cell is treated in the same way because \(a>\lambda _0/2\).  Geometric summation and ass:lower-shell-richness give total mass at most
\[
 c_-\lambda _0^\kappa+{c_-a^\kappa\over1-2^{-\kappa}}<1/2,
\]
so the higher-cell allocation is possible; for shells above the active range it is left unchanged.  This is the reservoir-rich allocation encoded by ass:lower-shell-richness and ass:upper-shell-richness.

The two richness inequalities also give the strict slack
\[
 \Delta:=c_+-2^\kappa c_->0.                                   \tag{20}
\]
Give the active dyadic reservoir a coefficient \(A>0\) so small that its baseline mass below \(v\leq s_0\) is at most \(Av^\kappa\) and
\[
 A2^\kappa\leq\Delta/2.                                       \tag{21}
\]
If an arbitrary fixed-sign propensity perturbation satisfies \(e/e_0\in[1/2,2]\) on that reservoir, then
\[
 \{u/2<e\leq u\}\subseteq\{u/4<e_0\leq2u\}.
\]
Consequently its entire active-reservoir contribution to the shell is at most
\[
 P_X\{u/4<e_0\leq2u,\ \text{active}\}
 \leq A(2u)^\kappa\leq{\Delta\over2}u^\kappa.                 \tag{22}
\]
The untouched background supplies the lower bound in (19), while (19), (20), and (22) give
\[
 P_X\{u/2<e\leq u\}
 \leq\left(2^\kappa c_-+{\Delta\over2}\right)u^\kappa
 <c_+u^\kappa                                                   \tag{23}
\]
whenever the active reservoir can enter the shell.  Its perturbed values are below \(2s_0\), so for \(u\geq4s_0\) it cannot enter \((u/2,u]\); those shells are unchanged and satisfy the original allocation.  Equations (19)--(23) therefore prove both shell inequalities for every fixed perturbation used below, not merely for its prior mixture.

Choose once and for all
\[
 0<s_c<s_0/2,\quad\quad 2s_c<s_0,
 \quad\quad B=\{s_c<e_0\leq2s_c\},\quad\quad m_*:=P_X(B)>0.           \tag{24}
\]
The last inequality follows from the positive active-reservoir coefficient.  All reservoirs are constructed with an auxiliary cell coordinate, so \(B\), and likewise every moving band below, can be divided into any finite number \(N\) of cells of equal \(P_X\)-mass without changing the propensity distribution.

For every family below generate \(D\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e(X))\), generate \((Y_0,Y_1)\) conditionally independently of \(D\) given \(X\), and put \(Y=DY_1+(1-D)Y_0\).  These choices verify ass:ignorability and ass:consistency.  Use centered Gaussian treated noise of variance \(0<\sigma^2\leq\sigma_1^2\wedge M_Y/4\) only in the mean-shift experiments, and zero residual noise otherwise.  All displayed regression amplitudes are multiplied by a common fixed \(c_A>0\).  Since \(r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en}\leq\bar r\), choose \(c_A\), using only the fixed class constants, so that
\[
 c_A\leq\min\{1/2,s_c\},
 \quad E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\leq M,
 \quad E_P[Y^2]\leq M_Y                                      \tag{25}
\]
in every family.  This is possible because each squared regression norm below is bounded by a fixed multiple of \(c_A^2\bar r^2\) or \(c_A^2\), and the residual variances already obey their stated envelopes.  Thus ass:bounded-treatment-effect-signal, ass:outcome-second-moment, ass:treated-residual-variance, and ass:control-residual-variance are verified by calibration rather than assumed of a construction.

We now construct the four rate channels.  The parametric part of the first channel uses two duplicated background cells of fixed positive mass and identical propensity.  Put the known treatment-effect signal equal to \(+c_A\) on one cell and \(-c_A\) on the other, keep all conditional laws and the exact public nuisances fixed, and transfer mass \(c_A/\sqrt n\) between the two cells in opposite directions.  The shell distribution is unchanged because the cells have the same propensity.  A direct categorical calculation gives one-row Kullback--Leibler divergence at most \(C c_A^2/n\), hence product divergence at most \(Cc_A^2\).  The elementary inequality \(\operatorname{TV}^2\leq\operatorname{KL}/2\), obtained by integrating \((\sqrt x-1)^2\leq (x-1)\log x/2\) and applying Cauchy--Schwarz, makes product total variation at most \(1/4\) after decreasing \(c_A\).  The target separation is a fixed multiple of \(n^{-1/2}\), so (17) proves the parametric obstruction.

For \(0<\kappa<1\) and \(r_{1n}>0\), first suppose
\[
 s=(nr_{1n}^2)^{-1}\leq s_0.
\]
On the active set \(A_s=\{e_0\leq s\}\), write \(m_s=P_X(A_s)\asymp s^\kappa\), and set
\[
 m_1=0,\quad p=e_0,\quad g_{1,\pm}=\pm h\mathbf 1_{A_s},
 \quad\quad h={c_A r_{1n}\over\sqrt{m_s}},                       \tag{26}
\]
with \(g_0=m_0=0\).  Then \(\|m_1-g_{1,\pm}\|_2=c_A r_{1n}\leq r_{1n}\).  Geometric summation of the active reservoir gives
\[
 E_P[e_0(X)\mathbf 1_{A_s}]\leq Csm_s.
\]
The Gaussian mean-shift likelihood therefore satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_+^n,P_-^n)
 ={2nh^2\over\sigma^2}E_P[e_0(X)\mathbf 1_{A_s}]
 \leq Cnh^2sm_s=Cc_A^2,                                     \tag{27}
\]
whereas
\[
 |\tau(P_+)-\tau(P_-)|=2hm_s
 \asymp r_{1n}s^{\kappa/2}
 =n^{-\kappa/2}r_{1n}^{1-\kappa}.                           \tag{28}
\]
If \(s>s_0\), then \(r_{1n}\leq s_0^{-1/2}n^{-1/2}\), so the right-hand side of (28) is at most a class-constant multiple of \(n^{-1/2}\), already covered by the parametric experiment.  If \(r_{1n}=0\), the nonparametric term vanishes and the same conclusion is immediate.

At \(\kappa=1\), put \(s=(nr_{1n}^2)^{-1}\) when \(r_{1n}>0\).  If \(s<s_0/2\), define
\[
 g_{1,\pm}=\pm {a_n\over e_0}\mathbf 1\{s\leq e_0\leq s_0\},
 \quad\quad a_n={c_A\over\sqrt{n\{1+\log(s_0/s)\}}}.           \tag{29}
\]
Because the active mass density is proportional to \(de_0\) at \(\kappa=1\), direct integration gives
\[
 \|g_{1,\pm}\|_2^2\leq C{a_n^2\over s}\leq Cc_A^2r_{1n}^2,
 \quad\quad
 \operatorname{KL}(P_+^n,P_-^n)
 \leq Cna_n^2\log(s_0/s)\leq Cc_A^2,                       \tag{30}
\]
and
\[
 |\tau(P_+)-\tau(P_-)|
 \geq ca_n\log(s_0/s)
 \asymp n^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+\log_+(nr_{1n}^2)}.                 \tag{31}
\]
The constant in (25) is decreased to absorb the fixed factor in the first inequality of (30).  When the interval in (29) is empty or has bounded logarithmic length, the expression in (31) is at most a constant multiple of the parametric floor.  For \(\kappa>1\), \(Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n})=n^{-1/2}\) by def:tail-noise-rate.  Equations (26)--(31), together with the parametric experiment, prove the entire \(Q_\kappa\) channel.

For the no-treated-observation channel, take
\[
 s=c_s n^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\leq s_0
\]
with a fixed sufficiently small \(c_s>0\), and use (26) on \(A_s\).  Couple the two observed samples identically unless an observation both lies in \(A_s\) and is treated.  A union bound and the active-tail calculation give
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_+^n,P_-^n)
 \leq nP\{X\in A_s,D=1\}
 \leq Cns^{\kappa+1}=Cc_s^{\kappa+1}.                       \tag{32}
\]
Choose \(c_s\) so that this is at most \(1/4\).  The target separation is
\[
 2hm_s\asymp r_{1n}s^{\kappa/2}
 \asymp r_{1n}n^{-\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]}.                    \tag{33}
\]
If \(s>s_0\), then \(n\) ranges over a fixed finite set; since \(r_{1n}\leq\bar r\), the quantity in (33) is bounded by a class-constant multiple of the parametric separation.  The case \(r_{1n}=0\) is again vacuous.

For the treated-side nuisance product, first suppose
\[
 s=c_s r_{en}^{2/(\kappa+2)}\leq s_0/2,
 \quad\quad B_s=\{s<e_0\leq2s\},
 \quad\quad m=P_X(B_s)\asymp s^\kappa.                           \tag{34}
\]
Divide \(B_s\) into \(N\) equal cells and draw independent signs with
\[
 \Pr_\theta(Z_j=z)={1+\theta\delta z\over2},
 \quad\quad \theta,z\in\{-1,1\},\quad\quad 0<\delta<1/4.            \tag{35}
\]
For every fixed \((\theta,Z)\), put
\[
 m_1=0,\quad p=e_0,\quad g_1=hZ_j\mathbf 1_{B_s},
 \quad e_{\theta,Z}={e_0\over1+\theta\delta Z_j},
 \quad h={c_A r_{1n}\over\sqrt m},                          \tag{36}
\]
and set the control regression and its public version to zero.  The propensity ratio lies in \([4/5,4/3]\subset[1/2,2]\); because \(e_0\leq2s\leq s_0<L/4\), positivity and right overlap follow.  Equations (22)--(23) prove both shell inequalities for every fixed-sign law.  Moreover,
\[
 \|m_1-g_1\|_2=c_A r_{1n}\leq r_{1n},
 \quad\quad
 \|p-e_{\theta,Z}\|_2
 \leq C\delta s\sqrt m\leq r_{en},                          \tag{37}
\]
where the last step follows from \(s\sqrt m\asymp s^{1+\kappa/2}=c_s^{1+\kappa/2}r_{en}\) after decreasing \(c_s\).  Thus every fixed law, not only the mixtures, is in \(\mathcal M_n\).

For a row in a cell whose sign has not previously appeared,
\[
 \Pr_\theta(Z_j=z)e_{\theta,z}
 ={1+\theta\delta z\over2}{e_0\over1+\theta\delta z}
 ={e_0\over2}.                                               \tag{38}
\]
The two treated-row mixtures, including their outcome distributions, are therefore identical.  Summing
\(
 \Pr_\theta(Z_j=z)(1-e_{\theta,z})=(1+\theta\delta z-e_0)/2
\)
over \(z\) also makes the control row identical.  Hence the two sample mixtures can differ only if two observations from \(B_s\) use the same cell, and
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(\overline P_+^n,\overline P_-^n)
 \leq {n(n-1)m^2\over2N}\leq {n(n-1)\over2N}.               \tag{39}
\]
Under prior \(\theta\),
\[
 \tau(P_{\theta,Z})={hm\over N}\sum_{j=1}^NZ_j,
 \quad E_\theta\tau(P_{\theta,Z})=\theta\delta hm,
 \quad \operatorname{Var}_\theta\{\tau(P_{\theta,Z})\}
 \leq {h^2m^2\over N}.                                      \tag{40}
\]
Taking \(N\) larger than fixed multiples of \(n^2\) and \(\delta^{-2}\) makes (39) and the Chebyshev failure probability for deviation \(\delta hm/2\) each at most \(1/16\).  The prior form of (17) then yields error of order
\[
 hm\asymp r_{1n}s^{\kappa/2}
 \asymp r_{1n}r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}.                   \tag{41}
\]
If the proposed \(s\) exceeds \(s_0/2\), use a fixed active band below \(s_0\).  Then \(r_{en}\) is bounded below by a fixed positive constant, the certificate in (37) is met after reducing the propensity tilt, and the separation is a constant multiple of \(r_{1n}\).  Since \(r_{en}\leq\bar r\), this dominates (41) up to a class-constant factor.

It remains to give the repaired control-side product family and to verify its fixed-sign membership.  Use exactly the fixed band \(B\) and mass \(m_*\) in (24), divide it into \(N\) equal cells, and, for every fixed \((\theta,Z)\), set on \(B\)
\[
 g_0=h_0Z_j,\quad\quad h_0={c_A r_{0n}\over\sqrt{m_*}},
 \quad\quad m_0=0,\quad\quad p=e_0,
 \quad\quad 1-e_{\theta,Z}={1-e_0\over1+\theta tZ_j},            \tag{42}
\]
where
\[
 t=c_A\min\left\{{r_{en}\over\sqrt{m_*}},{1\over4}\right\}.
                                                                    \tag{43}
\]
Outside \(B\), leave \(e=e_0\), and take \(g_1=m_1=0\).  Bias the cell signs according to
\[
 \Pr_\theta(Z_j=z)={1+\theta tz\over2}.                     \tag{44}
\]
By (25) and (43), \(t\leq c_A/4\leq s_c/4\).  Writing \(a=\theta tZ_j\), direct algebra gives
\[
 e_{\theta,Z}={e_0+a\over1+a},
 \quad\quad {e_{\theta,Z}\over e_0}
 =1+{a(1-e_0)\over e_0(1+a)}.                               \tag{45}
\]
Since \(e_0>s_c\) and \(|a|\leq t\leq s_c/4\),
\[
 {3\over4}\leq {e_{\theta,Z}\over e_0}\leq {5\over4},    \tag{46}
\]
and this interval is contained in \([1/2,2]\).  In particular, the numerator in (45) is at least \(e_0-t>3s_c/4>0\), proving positivity.  Also
\[
 e_{\theta,Z}\leq {5\over4}e_0\leq {5\over2}s_c
 <{5\over4}s_0<{5\over16}L<L,                               \tag{47}
\]
which proves ass:right-overlap.  Equations (22)--(23) apply by (46), so both dyadic shell inequalities hold for every fixed \((\theta,Z)\).

The propensity difference in (45) satisfies
\[
 |e_{\theta,Z}-e_0|={t(1-e_0)\over|1+a|}\leq{t\over1-t}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \|e_{\theta,Z}-p\|_2
 \leq {t\sqrt{m_*}\over1-t}\leq r_{en}.                    \tag{48}
\]
For the last inequality, if \(r_{en}/\sqrt{m_*}\leq1/4\), use \(t=c_A r_{en}/\sqrt{m_*}\) and \(c_A/(1-c_A/4)\leq1\); if \(r_{en}/\sqrt{m_*}>1/4\), use \(t=c_A/4\), \(r_{en}>\sqrt{m_*}/4\), and the same bound.  Furthermore,
\[
 \|g_0-m_0\|_2=h_0\sqrt{m_*}=c_A r_{0n}\leq r_{0n},         \tag{49}
\]
while the treated regression and public function coincide.  Equations (25), (48), and (49), together with the causal construction preceding (25), verify every remaining condition defining \(\mathcal M_n\) for each fixed-sign law.

The cancellation is exact.  For the control row, including its outcome \(Y=g_0=h_0z\),
\[
 \Pr_\theta(Z_j=z)(1-e_{\theta,z})
 ={1+\theta tz\over2}{1-e_0\over1+\theta tz}
 ={1-e_0\over2}.                                             \tag{50}
\]
For a treated row, whose outcome law is unchanged because \(g_1=0\),
\[
 \sum_{z\in\{-1,1\}}\Pr_\theta(Z_j=z)e_{\theta,z}
 =\sum_{z\in\{-1,1\}}{e_0+\theta tz\over2}=e_0.           \tag{51}
\]
Thus unseen-cell one-row mixtures agree under \(\theta=1\) and \(\theta=-1\).  As in (39), their sample-mixture total variation is at most \(n(n-1)m_*^2/(2N)\).  The random target is
\[
 \tau(P_{\theta,Z})=-{h_0m_*\over N}\sum_{j=1}^NZ_j,
\]
so its center and variance are
\[
 E_\theta\tau(P_{\theta,Z})=-\theta th_0m_*,
 \quad\quad
 \operatorname{Var}_\theta\{\tau(P_{\theta,Z})\}
 \leq {h_0^2m_*^2\over N}.                                  \tag{52}
\]
Choose \(N\) larger than fixed multiples of \(n^2\) and \(t^{-2}\) when \(t>0\).  The collision probability and the Chebyshev probability of deviation greater than \(th_0m_*/2\) are then each at most \(1/16\).  If \(t=0\), the desired product term is zero and no control family is needed.  The half-separation of the two prior centers is exactly
\[
 d_0=th_0m_*
 =c_A^2r_{0n}\min\{r_{en},\sqrt{m_*}/4\}.                    \tag{53}
\]
In the small branch this equals \(c_A^2r_{0n}r_{en}\).  In the large branch, \(r_{en}>\sqrt{m_*}/4\), and the fixed cap \(r_{en}\leq\bar r\) gives
\[
 d_0={c_A^2\sqrt{m_*}\over4}r_{0n}
 \geq {c_A^2\sqrt{m_*}\over4\bar r}r_{0n}r_{en}.           \tag{54}
\]
Thus (17), (50)--(54), and the fixed-sign membership just proved yield the \(r_{0n}r_{en}\) obstruction.

We have constructed in \(\mathcal M_n\), with identical public functions within each subexperiment, testing obstructions for
\[
 Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n}),\quad\quad
 r_{1n}n^{-\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]},\quad\quad
 r_{1n}r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)},\quad\quad
 r_{0n}r_{en}.                                                \tag{55}
\]
The first displayed quantity includes the parametric alternative.  The sum of the four nonnegative quantities is at most four times their maximum.  After decreasing a class-constant threshold and taking the minimum of the positive testing probabilities, (17) gives constants \(c>0\) and \(\delta_0\in(0,1/4)\), independent of \(n\) and the admissible radius triple, such that every \(T\in\mathcal T_n\) obeys
\[
 \sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n}
 P\{|T-\tau(P)|\geq c\rho_n\}\geq\delta_0.                 \tag{56}
\]
Allowing \(T\) to use the public functions and certified radii cannot distinguish the hypotheses because those inputs are identical inside each family.

On the event in (56), absolute loss is at least \(c\rho_n\) and squared loss is at least \(c^2\rho_n^2\).  Taking expectations, then the supremum over \(\mathcal M_n\), and finally the infimum over \(\mathcal T_n\) in def:absolute-risk and def:root-mse-risk yields
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{(1)}\geq c\delta_0\rho_n,
 \quad\quad
 \mathfrak R_n^{(2)}\geq c\sqrt{\delta_0}\rho_n.
\]
This proves every assertion of the theorem, including membership of every fixed-sign law and its signal-moment calibration.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Build four subexperiments inside \(\mathcal M_n\): shell-localized treated-mean shifts for \(Q_{\kappa}\), an untreated-observation coupling at scale \(n^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\), a signed-cell fuzzy mixture at scale \(r_{en}^{2/(\kappa+2)}\) whose propensity tilt cancels its sign tilt in each treated observed row, and a control-side fuzzy mixture on a fixed band \(B=\{s_c<e_0\le 2s_c\}\) of the same perturbable active tail reservoir. For the control family, split \(B\) into \(N\) equal cells, put \(g_0=h_0Z_j\), \(h_0=c_A r_{0n}/\sqrt{P_X(B)}\), publicly supply \(m_0=0\) and \(p=e_0\), and set \(1-e_{\theta,Z}=(1-e_0)/(1+\theta tZ_j)\), where \(t=c_A\min\{r_{en}/\sqrt{P_X(B)},1/4\}\). Choose \(c_A\) from the fixed class constants so that every fixed-sign law preserves positivity, right overlap, both dyadic shell inequalities, the nuisance certificates, and the signal and outcome moments. In every family keep the public functions fixed across the hypotheses, bound mixture discrepancy by cell collisions, concentrate the random target, and combine the four component separations into \(\rho_n\) by the maximum-to-sum comparison.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The former construction left the control fuzzy family on an unspecified regular cell and did not discharge right overlap or shell membership for every fixed sign. The corrected construction moves that family to a fixed band of the already shell-calibrated active reservoir and records the exact control-row cancellation and radius scaling.

proposed.citation: Heiler, P., and Kazak, E. (2021). Extreme propensity scores and non-Gaussian limits for IPW and doubly robust estimators. Journal of Econometrics.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Restore the failed parent run's bibliography record so the mandated extreme-propensity limit-law comparator can be stated without a dangling key.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives the parametric-plus-nuisance-product structure-agnostic treatment-effect rate under a propensity bounded away from zero.
Section 2 gives the pure structure-agnostic ATE benchmark consisting of the parametric floor plus the nuisance-product rate under regular overlap.
Thresholded AIPW is uniformly asymptotically normal under sufficient weak-overlap nuisance conditions.
IPW has Gaussian or stable limits according to tail and trimming regimes.
Extreme propensity scores generate non-Gaussian limit theory for IPW and doubly robust estimators.
Localized fuzzy hypotheses yield a minimax lower bound for pointwise CATE.
Inverse-weight estimation can have tail-dependent irregular rates.
Limited-overlap confidence accuracy is driven by local comparison-cell sizes.
Section 6.1 treats bounded-overlap ATE examples, while the conclusion identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as an open extension.

Theorem 3.1 gives asymptotic linearity and a studentized Gaussian limit for bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimators targeting the original treatment-effect estimand, with Proposition B.1 verifying the ATE specialization.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The decision review requires the Heiler--Kazak extreme-propensity comparator and an explicit statement that its limit-law contribution is informative rather than matched by the present minimax theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The smallest adaptation penalty and its matching lower bound when the tail exponent, both shell constants, and all three nuisance radii are unknown.
open_obligations.obstruction: The proved oracle threshold uses the unknown quantities in three competing scales. The frozen adaptation handle does not specify observable confidence bounds for the global approximation errors, and the fixed certificates used in the oracle proof cannot be recovered uniformly from a validation sample without additional structure on the public predictors. Honest interval adaptation also requires a between-class testing argument not supplied by the fixed-index lower families.
open_obligations.attempted: A dyadic Lepski comparison controls stochastic differences between clipped scores, but its deterministic clipping biases contain \(r_{1n}\lambda^{\kappa/2}\), \(r_{1n}r_{en}/\lambda\), and \(r_{0n}r_{en}\), none of which has a uniformly estimable upper certificate under the frozen model. Empirical shell counts estimate the observed propensity tail only after controlling the unknown propensity approximation error, which is the same unidentified radius entering the choice.
open_obligations.partial_result: With \(\kappa\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), and the certified radii supplied, thm:clipped-absolute-upper, lem:median-risk-upgrade, and thm:honest-interval-frontier attain risk and expected length of order \(\rho_n\), so the oracle adaptation penalty is \(1\). No claim about the unknown-index penalty follows from the frozen primitives.

project_justification.fill: The core supplies an explicit public-information decision class, bounded nuisance radii, a fixed treatment-effect signal moment envelope, one clipped estimator, median amplification, and four fixed-sign-valid converse channels. The repaired control-product channel is constructed on a fixed band of the perturbable active tail reservoir, where positivity, right overlap, both dyadic shell inequalities, nuisance membership, collision control, and exact mixture cancellation are verified before it is combined with the other channels. The polynomial deterioration threshold and an oracle bias-aware interval are indexed by \(\rho_n\).

prose_updates.related_work: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1 and Remark 2, is the closest public-function experiment: it gives the doubly robust structure-agnostic rate when the propensity is bounded away from zero, and its asymmetric fuzzy hypotheses inform the dyadic-reservoir converse. BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, Section 2, studies pure and smoothness-augmented black-box classes under regular overlap. The shell class is disjoint from the bounded-overlap public-function class, but Proposition 8 shows that its fast-tail rate limit retains \(r_{1n}/\sqrt n\) and is uniformly equivalent, under \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\), to their parametric-plus-product benchmark. JinSyrgkanis2025GeneralLinearFunctionalLowerBounds, Section 6.1 and the conclusion, broadens structure-agnostic lower bounds while retaining bounded-overlap ATE examples and expressly identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as open; it supplies the regime-opening anchor rather than a theorem matched here. Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics gives a clipped cross-fitted AIPW Gaussian limit under sufficient tail and nuisance conditions; it informs the upper score but is not a risk comparator. MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1, constructs a bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimator that preserves the original ATE and establishes asymptotic linearity and normal inference; it does not give the global-\(L^2\) public-function minimax-risk frontier or the matching honest-length converse. MaWang2020RobustIPW derives Gaussian and stable IPW limits and selects a trimming threshold from the sample for its own IPW criterion. HeilerKazak2021ExtremePropensity develops non-Gaussian limit theory for IPW and doubly robust estimators under extreme propensity scores. Those limit-law results address irregular inference, whereas the present result matches global-\(L^2\) minimax absolute risk, root mean-squared risk, fixed-probability error, and honest expected length. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE provides the localized fuzzy-hypothesis method for a different estimand and smoothness class. KhanTamer2010Irregular explains why support tails govern inverse-weight rates. Rothe2017RobustCI motivates local effective sample size and limited-overlap coverage, but its robust intervals rely on finite-cell or auxiliary distributional structure rather than the four-channel global-\(L^2\) radius.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The lower frontier is restricted to reservoir-rich fixed shell constants satisfying ass:lower-shell-richness and ass:upper-shell-richness. Each lower family calibrates its regression perturbation to satisfy ass:bounded-treatment-effect-signal. In the repaired control-product family, the perturbation is supported on the fixed active-reservoir band \(B=\{s_c<e_0\le2s_c\}\): every fixed sign has propensity ratio in \([3/4,5/4]\), preserves positivity and right overlap, consumes at most half of the shell slack \(\Delta=c_+-2^\kappa c_-\), and obeys both global \(L^2(P_X)\) certificates. The upper bound needs only uniform shells and the fixed signal moment, so arbitrarily tight admissible shell constants may have a different converse geometry.

statement_notes.justification: This shell-matching converse certifies all four obstructions against the full public-information decision class, with the repaired control channel verified law by law on a fixed active-tail band.
statement_notes.gap: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR and KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE provide fuzzy-hypothesis templates, but not the shell-preserving collision, empty-treatment, and fixed-band control channels for this ATE experiment.
statement_notes.consumer: The lower bound certifies that no estimator using the sample and the same public predictions can remove any rate component; thm:sharp-four-risk-frontier and thm:honest-interval-frontier consume the corrected fixed-sign-valid converse.

statement_notes.justification: It closes the exact global-prediction price of one-sided weak overlap across three operational loss criteria by combining the feasible estimators with the repaired four-channel converse.
statement_notes.gap: The closest regular-overlap benchmarks are JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR and BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE; HeilerKazak2021ExtremePropensity studies non-Gaussian limit behavior rather than this matched global-\(L^2\) minimax frontier.
statement_notes.consumer: Method developers can use the theorem as the oracle benchmark for clipping, robustification, and any proposed higher-order correction.
